newsitem.title: CHINA: Bayer AG sees China sales doubling.
newsitem.headline: Bayer AG sees China sales doubling.

text.p: German chemical and drugs group Bayer AG sees sales in China doubling to over $1 billion in the next 10 years, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Bayer hopes to boost sales by localising manufacturing and investing heavily in China, the newspaper said. The company's gross sales in China and Hong Kong totalled $520 million last year, up 15 percent from the previous year.
The group's total investment in China would rise to at least $350 million, Bayer chairman Michale Portoff was quoted as saying.

It has pledged to invest $150 million in eight joint ventures with Chinese partners, the newspaper said. Two of the joint ventures are in operation, while the rest will be put into operation before early 1998.
The ventures will manufacture flavours and fragrances, colour film, dispersion dyes, iron oxide, rubber, pharmaceuticals and animal health care products, it said.
Combined sales of the joint ventures are estimated at $200 million by the year 2000, Portoff said. The ventures will create more than 1,000 jobs.
Bayer is conducting negotiations to establish another six ventures involving investment of $200 million, he said.
